diffs.diff: header pin 1: part says GND, datasheet reading says VM
diffs.evidence: SparkFun ROB-14450 v11 board file: header JP1 (1X08, rot R90, pad 1 at y=1.27 mm) nets are pad1=GND, pad2=B01, pad3=B02, pad4=A02, pad5=A01, pad6=GND, pad7=VCC, pad8=VM; silkscreen on that row reads VM (y=19.5) VCC GND A01 A02 B02 B01 GND (y=1.7) from top to bottom. The second reading listed the same labels in top-to-bottom silkscreen order (VM first, and 'AO'/'BO' with letter O instead of the printed A01/B01), i.e. the reverse of the connector's real pin numbering; the model follows the board's actual pad numbers, so every physical position/label pairing is identical. Board file: <contactref element="JP1" pad="1"/> is on signal GND.

diffs.diff: minimum supply: part 2.7 V, datasheet reading 4.5 V
diffs.evidence: Toshiba TB6612FNG datasheet, Operating Range: 'Supply voltage VCC 2.7 (min) 3 (typ) 5.5 (max) V; VM 2.5 5 13.5 V'; output current 1.0 A for 'VM >= 4.5 V', lower for '4.5 V > VM >= 2.5 V'. The model's vmin/vmax describe the logic supply VCC (2.7-5.5 V) that the microcontroller connects to; 4.5 V is only the VM level for full output current (application circuit '+4.5 V to 13.5 V'), not the chip's minimum supply.
